title: Management of Primary Dysmenorrhea and Pelvic Pain
summary: Primary dysmenorrhea is primarily mediated by excessive uterine prostaglandin F2alpha synthesis. First-line pharmacotherapy includes targeted prostaglandin synthase inhibitors (NSAIDs) initiated 24-48 hours prior to expected menses.

interventions.name: Magnesium Bisglycinate Supplementation
interventions.biological_mechanism: Smooth muscle uterine myometrial relaxation, reduced prostaglandin F2a production, NMDA receptor downregulation.

interventions.name: Continuous Low-Level Topical Heat Therapy
interventions.dosage_instructions: Continuous abdominal heat wrap (40°C) for 8 hours
interventions.biological_mechanism: Vasodilation of pelvic microvasculature, reduction of uterine ischemia and visceral spasm.

interventions.name: Zingiber Officinale (Ginger Rhizome) Extract
interventions.dosage_instructions: 250mg standardized ginger powder four times daily for first 3 days of menses
interventions.biological_mechanism: Cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase inhibition equivalent to ibuprofen in controlled trials.

title: Diagnosis and Metabolic Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
summary: PCOS is characterized by hyperandrogenism, chronic oligo-anovulation, and insulin resistance causing extended follicular arrest and high cycle variance.

interventions.name: Myo-Inositol and D-Chiro-Inositol Formulation
interventions.biological_mechanism: Restores insulin signaling cascade in granulosa cells, reduces serum free testosterone, and normalizes LH/FSH ratio to induce spontaneous regular ovulation.

interventions.name: Low-Glycemic Index & Anti-Inflammatory Dietary Protocol
interventions.dosage_instructions: Macronutrient distribution: 40% low-GI carbs, 30% lean protein, 30% healthy monounsaturated fats
interventions.biological_mechanism: Blunts postprandial hyperinsulinemia, reducing ovarian theca cell androgen hypersecretion.

title: Circadian Rhythm Deficits and Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Ovarian (HPO) Axis Dysregulation
summary: Circadian phase shifting and sleep deficits < 6.5 hours impair nocturnal LH pulsatility and elevate evening cortisol, directly delaying follicular recruitment.

interventions.name: Circadian Entrainment & Morning Melatonin Suppression Protocol
interventions.dosage_instructions: 10,000 lux natural or daylight lamp exposure within 30 min of waking; dark room 2h before bed
interventions.biological_mechanism: Suprachiasmatic nucleus synchronization, stabilizing GnRH pulse generator and preventing stress-induced cycle phase elongation.

interventions.name: L-Theanine & Ashwagandha (Withania Somnifera) Adaptogenic Blend
interventions.biological_mechanism: Reduces adrenocortical cortisol velocity, preventing HPA-axis disruption of ovulation.

title: Management of Premenstrual Syndrome and Late Luteal Symptoms
summary: Late luteal affective and somatic distress stems from heightened sensitivity to rapid progesterone withdrawal and allopregnanolone GABA-A receptor modulation.

interventions.name: Vitex Agnus-Castus (Chasteberry Extract)
interventions.dosage_instructions: 20mg - 40mg standardized extract once daily in the morning
interventions.biological_mechanism: Dopaminergic agonist action at pituitary D2 receptors, suppressing latent hyperprolactinemia and stabilizing luteal progesterone synthesis.

interventions.name: Pyridoxal-5-Phosphate (Active Vitamin B6) & Calcium Carbonate
interventions.dosage_instructions: 50mg P-5-P + 1000mg Calcium daily during luteal phase
interventions.biological_mechanism: Cofactor in serotonin and dopamine synthesis; calcium attenuates neurovascular water retention and mood lability.
